newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss slap mad cow limits on beef imports.
newsitem.headline: Swiss slap mad cow limits on beef imports.

text.p: Switzerland, whose beef exports have been banned by Germany and other states due to fears of mad cow disease, will limit beef imports from Europe from January 1 for health reasons.

Swiss Federal Veterinary Office director Ulrich Kihm told Swiss radio on Friday the new rule will require imports of beef products be guaranteed free of internal organs and nerve tissue, which are considered most likely to spread mad cow disease.
This will effectively block imports of beef products such as sausage from Germany as well as Austria and Italy, all neighbours who have banned or restriced imports of Swiss beef.
After Britain, Switzerland has the highest number of cases of Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy (BSE), commonly known as mad cow disease. The report of three cases last week brought the total to 230.
But Kihm denied on Swiss public radio DRS that his office's action was retribution for the bans on Swiss beef.
"We want to avoid the risk from (cattle) organs and tissues such as brain, spinal column material and spleen," Kihm said.
Kihm said a Swiss survey had found that BSE monitoring in European Union countries was insuffiencient.
BSE is suspected transmitter of the brain-wasting Creuzfeldt-Jakob Disease (CJD) which affects humans.
Kihm said the Swiss ban would also restrict imports of whole cows, sheep and goats to countries that, like Switzerland, ban animals being fed the processed cadavers of their own kind.
Switzerland, which is not a European Union member, told its European trade partners of its decision on Thursday.
